In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites tonight, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . NC State -6.5 NC State first half -3.5 NC State vs Stanford prop: NC State team total Over 31.5 After a shaky start to the year, CJ Bailey has been far more impressive in his last few starts. He's put up a 72+ QBR in four of the Wolfpack's last five games and should continue to play well enough for NC State to hit its team total Over at 32.5 or better . In his last three outings, he's finished with an adjusted completion percentage of 77.1% or higher while accounting for just two turnover-worthy plays. His efficiency has helped the Wolfpack climb to 37th nationally in pass success rate (47.6%) , which doesn't bode well for Stanford. The Cardinal allow the eighth-most passing yards per game in the Power Four (255.4) and are the only P4 program with fewer than five sacks and fewer than five interceptions. A historically bad play against a lousy Vanderbilt team here, and a 38-14 home loss to a red-hot Wake Forest there, and now the Wolfpack need this. However, win, and there's a chance to go on a big second-half run with a favorable schedule. Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. NC State only has one game – at Florida State – outside of North Carolina the rest of the way, hosting Cal, Duke, and Syracuse next. The two programs have only met once. The lack of a pass rush and few defensive stops are the real issues, but you can't win if you don't score, and Stanford can't put the biscuit in the basket. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. away.blurb: Head coach Dave Doeren said Monday that offensive lineman Yousef Mugharbil and tight end Vander Ploog are out for the season. Mugharbil sustained a lower leg injury during the Wolfpack’s 31-28 win over Louisville. He recorded a 64.4 offensive grade, according to Pro Football Focus, which was third on the offensive line. Mugharbil also graded out at 70 in pass blocking. The former transfer walk-on put together his best season of college football, earning a career-high 339 snaps. Ploog, a sophomore transfer from Oregon, played eight snaps against Virginia and one against Richmond. He came to Raleigh with a nagging shoulder injury, Doeren said, and could not get healthy. He will be able to return, but it won’t be until after the conclusion of this season. Ploog was spotted prior to the bye week leaving practice in a sling. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era at Michigan will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Michigan Football vs. Indiana With Tommy Carr Under Center Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Very little has come easy for Michigan this season. The Wolverines needed a second Hail Mary attempt to beat Western Michigan, a final stop to take down Oklahoma, and a final stop to beat Penn State . Add in a game-winning touchdown pass by Iowa and Michigan has been on both sides of winning and losing on a play. And things likely don't get any easier whatsoever this weekend. Not only will Michigan host Indiana , the reigning national champions, but the Hoosiers come into Ann Arbor hungry . Indiana suffered its first loss since the 2024 season last weekend after Ohio State won by inches. Michigan is set to turn the ball over to Tommy Carr, who replaced Bryce Underwood in the second half last week against Penn State. How will Carr and the Wolverines fare against Curt Cignetti's team? Michigan on SI predicts the outcome. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect I really think Michigan's defense can hold its own against Indiana, and I wouldn't believe the Hoosiers are going to roll into Ann Arbor and win going away. While the Wolverines' defense is legit, so is Indiana's. The problem for me going into this game is that we have no idea what to expect from Tommy Carr. I really think Michigan's defense can hold its own against Indiana, and I wouldn't believe the Hoosiers are going to roll into Ann Arbor and win going away. While the Wolverines' defense is legit, so is Indiana's. The problem for me going into this game is that we have no idea what to expect from Tommy Carr. The freshman certainly sparked Michigan's offense last weekend, but the Wolverines didn't ask much from Carr. He sparked the offensive line and running game to play better. If that happens this weekend, Michigan has a fighter's chance. But I believe Indiana will make Carr beat it. Making your first start against the Hoosiers is a tall task, and I'm guessing Michigan's offense doesn't score enough points to win this game. In addition, they’ll be looking to build on last week’s 21-18 win over the Penn State Nittany Lions with a new quarterback. Tommy Carr will make his first career start after replacing Bryce Underwood last week and giving the offense a spark. Indiana should be re-focused coming off a loss against the Ohio State Buckeyes by mere blades of grass. We’ve looked into our crystal ball to determine what exactly is going to happen. Will Michigan be able to pull off the upset? Savion Hiter Breaks a Big Run Michigan’s run game is going to be the focal point of the offense in Saturday’s game. Last week, Bryson Kuzdzal broke off the big run that got Michigan into the end zone for the first time. Explosive plays in the run game have been too few and far between. Bryce Underwood gets benched and all of a sudden Savion Hiter is really good. pic.twitter.com/fK2RPVg08d Going into play last week, Michigan had just one run for more than 20 yards. That was Bryce Underwood’s 38-yard touchdown against Oklahoma in the second game of the season. Last week, Kuzdzal had one big run, as did Savion Hiter. Hiter has been so close to breaking off a long run this season. A shoestring tackle or a missed assignment have gotten in the way. This week, we’re predicting that everything will finally come together for a big run for Hiter. He breaks off another run of more than 40 yards for the second consecutive week as he joins the lineup after watching Jordan Marshall punish the opposing defense. Since returning to the lineup for conference play, Hogan Hansen has shown some life for this group. He has some good chemistry with Tommy Carr and showed off some pass catching ability last week once Carr was in the game. picks.blurb: Michigan football vs Indiana predictions, picks in Big Ten game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Brewers' stunning comeback Valkyries even WNBA Finals Kimi Antonelli on US GP pole NFL injury updates Tatum downplays beef Michigan football vs Indiana predictions, picks in Big Ten game Jeff Seidel, Shawn Windsor, Carlos Monarrez, Rainer Sabin and Tony Garcia, Detroit Free Press Sat, October 24, 2026 at 9:01 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines enter this week feeling good after taking down Penn State amid a quarterback swap, going from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr. Now, the true freshman gets his first start, and it will not be an easy one. Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten ) just lost its first game after a 22-game win streak, losing by inches to Ohio State. Michigan (4-2, 1-2) will likely need to lean on its mighty defense to hand the Hoosiers their first losing streak in the Curt Cignetti era. Can the Wolverines pull off the upset against IU football? Our five experts make their predictions: Call me crazy. Call it a wild hunch that goes against all the betting experts. But Michigan has a tremendous defense. And I firmly believe that if you just give the Wolverines some mistake-free offense, they can play with anybody. With Tommy Carr at QB, it changes everything for Michigan. If the defense can force a few turnovers (granted, I know, that's super hard against Indiana) and if Carr can avoid mistakes, the Wolverines can pull off a huge upset. The pick: Michigan 23, Indiana 20. [ MUST LISTEN: Make "Hail Yes!" your go-to Wolverines podcast, available anywhere you listen to podcasts ( Apple , Spotify ) or watch live/on demand on YouTube . ] Carlos Monarrez The Tommy Carr era is expected to officially start. But it's going to be rough sledding because the Curt Cignetti era has been going strong for a while and surely motivated to bounce back after a tough loss to Ohio State. Just consider a turnover-free game and a couple of touchdown drives a moral victory for Carr and the Wolverines. The pick: Indiana 31, Michigan 19. Shawn Windsor Tommy Carr gets his first official start, and against most other teams the uptick in offense would be easy to spot. It'll be harder to spot against the Hoosiers defense. Fortunately, Indiana isn't the offensive machine it was a year ago, and U-M's defense will keep it in the game until the fourth quarter. The pick: Indiana 23, Michigan 16 It's hard to believe, but over the last three seasons, Indiana has been a much better program than Michigan. The Hoosiers now have championship DNA, and it will be evident on Saturday when their stingy defense – ranked among the nation's best – puts the clamps on the Tommy Carr-led Wolverines. While Carr gives Michigan's offense some more juice, it won't be enough to outscore a team that remains a legitimate title contender. The pick: Indiana 24, Michigan 20. Indiana hasn't lost consecutive games in the Curt Cignetti era, which dates back more than two-and-a-half years. The Hoosiers also haven't lost the turnover battle in the past 31 games. U-M has continued to shoot itself in the foot, which was the main reason it made a switch at quarterback. While the hope is this operation will be cleaner, there's no guarantee. IU has given up more than 17 points once this year. It's hard to imagine this offense will be the one to break any of those streaks. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals IU Why Curt Cignetti stuck with injured Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover in win at Michigan Michael Niziolek The Herald-Times Updated Oct. 24, 2026, 5:47 p.m. ET Indiana defeated Michigan 13-6 in overtime despite offensive struggles in the second half. Quarterback Josh Hoover played through an injury, completing only one pass after halftime. Coach Curt Cignetti considered replacing Hoover but ultimately decided to stick with him. ANN ARBOR, MI — Indiana football coach Curt Cignetti admitted the staff had a "lot of discussions" about replacing Josh Hoover in the second half of a 13-6 overtime win over Michigan on Saturday. While Hoover wasn't listed on IU's availability report leading into the game, he wasn't 100% from an apparent injury he suffered against Ohio State. The No. 6 Hoosiers (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten) put up only 49 yards of total offense in the second half with Hoover only attempting two passes during that stretch. Late in the third quarter, Michigan scored its first points of the game after intercepting one of those attempts deep inside Indiana territory. Cignetti considered pulling Hoover for backup Grant Wilson throughout the second half, but opted against it. This was only the second time in Hoover's career that he didn't complete at least 50% of his passes in a single game and the first time in 10 games that he didn't throw at least one passing touchdown. He finished 8 of 18 for 81 yards with an interception. "We found a way to get it done," Cignetti said. "And probably surprised them with our decoy Brock Schott down the seam. And then who would have ever thought we'd run Josh down there for a touchdown? The element of surprise is still alive in college football."

away.headline: Michigan football availability report vs Indiana: Yet another OL is out
away.blurb: Tackle Blake Frazier, who opened the season on the left side before Andrew Sprague was lost and U-M flipped him to the right side, is out, per the Big Ten's game day availability report . He's been a mainstay on an offensive line that's now using its sixth iteration through seven games. Michigan will have former five-star Andrew Babalola available, and he could possibly see the first action of his career. If so, coach Kyle Whittingham likes him on the left side. That could mean Michigan bumps Evan Link back into left guard (where he started the year) and would need to make a decision at right tackle; that could be the versatile Brady Norton or possibly true freshman Marky Walbridge. The other notable updates: safety Rod Moore and Enow Etta are both listed as game-time decisions. Moore, a three-time captain, left last week's 21-18 win over Penn State after recording a diving interception, before he went to the medical tent and was subsequently carted up the tunnel. He's been listed as questionable all week, and his status was on the fence. Etta did not leave last week's game with any clear injury and spoke with media postgame but has been listed as questionable since the first report came out on Wednesday. Michigan has primarily rotated three defensive tackles with Etta, Trey Pierce and Jonah Lea'ea. If Etta can't go, it would likely mean more time for Bobby Kanka or Deyvid Palepale, both of whom have been fighting for the fourth and fifth spots. The only other players who are out were all expected including Sprague, tight end Mason Bonner and wide receiver Kendrick Bell among the players who've seen time this season. There's also a chance U-M flips Link to the right side and starts Nathan Efobi and Avery Gach at the two guard spots. In any event, it will be a new combination up front protecting true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr, who is expected to make his first career start. away.headline: How Josh Hoover played through pain to lead Indiana football to overtime win at Michigan
away.blurb: “Regardless of how I felt, there's guys on this team that are banged up every week, right?” Hoover said. “It’s no different for me versus anybody else. Like we're all gonna do what we can to be out here and be at our best and try to help our team win. That's what it comes down to.” “No matter what's going on or what's happened, like in those moments, you just gotta block everything out and go focus on the next play and go win in the game,” Hoover said. “That’s what matters.” “It was a tough week,” Hoover said. “Obviously, this is a physical league and you're here, that's something that everybody goes through, right? I think people don't sometimes understand what it looks like to come out here and play every single week. Like there's gonna be weeks where you don't feel good.” Cignetti opted against making a change with Hoover as determined as ever to help his team pull out the win. “We're in it together no matter what happens,” Hoover said. “And we're gonna go out there, just like we did today, and do what we can for our brothers.” ANN ARBOR, MI — Indiana football quarterback Josh Hoover did what he felt any of his teammates would do in the same situation. Battling through an undisclosed injury, Hoover scored the go-ahead touchdown in a 13-6 overtime win over Michigan on Saturday at The Big House. He absorbed contact at the goal line and plunged into the end zone to keep IU ’s playoff hopes alive and well. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. He completed fewer than 50% of his pass attempts, finished with less than 100 passing yards for the first time as a starter and threw a costly interception (his first of the season) that nearly allowed Michigan to take a lead. Indiana had just 49 total yards with two first downs in the second half with IU reluctant to even try and attempt a pass. Hanging over all that, Hoover acknowledged “battling through some things” health-wise throughout the week thanks to an awkward hit he took on his throwing arm in a 19-15 loss to Ohio State . While Hoover missed only one snap against the Buckeyes, the broadcast captured close-up footage of him in obvious pain trying to throw the ball . He still hasn’t discussed the exact nature of the injury, but wasn’t at 100% when the game against Michigan kicked off on Saturday. It got the point though where his obvious struggles had the coaching staff contemplating a change . Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to duplicate that performance against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. Where to watch LSU vs. Auburn live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Jordan-Hare Stadium -- Auburn, Alabama TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. LSU vs. Auburn prediction, picks What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double-digits. Our college football expert expects a low-scoring Tiger Bowl and breaks down the best betting angles. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Sam Leavitt of LSU and Byrum Brown of Auburn. Auburn may look like an attractive home dog following last week's upset, but our LSU vs. Auburn prediction prioritize the macro-level mismatch. LSU's defense and net EPA profile lead the nation, whereas Auburn's offense is forced to operate through Byrum Brown carrying the load solo. Check out why we're laying the points with LSU and locking in the Under for Saturday's matchup in our latest college football picks for Week 8. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup, and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn prop: LSU over 3.5 touchdowns LSU has scored 36 offensive touchdowns through seven games, and Auburn's profile points toward repeat scoring opportunities. The home defense allows a 45.2% success rate, sitting 85th nationally, while generating havoc on only 15.8% of snaps . Leavitt owns a 55% passing success rate, giving LSU an efficient way to remain ahead of schedule and avoid settling for long field goals. Trey'Dez Green 's removal from the injury report also gives Kiffin his 6-foot-7 red-zone target back. Auburn can make LSU work through full drives, but it has not consistently produced the negative plays needed to keep those drives out of the end zone. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. Ryan Minion Sat, October 24, 2026 at 2:32 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers take on the Auburn Tigers in Auburn, Alabama, on Saturday, Oct 24. Kickoff is set for 12 p.m. ET on ABC. LSU is favored by -7.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -310. Auburn, meanwhile, enters as a +7.5 underdog and is +245 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 50.5 total points. Here's my LSU vs. Auburn prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 24. LSU vs. Auburn Odds, Spread, Pick LSU vs. Auburn Pick: Both Teams to Score 20+ Points (-117) My Auburn vs. LSU best bet is on both teams to score at least 20 points. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . LSU Tigers Betting Preview LSU enters its Week 8 matchup against Auburn with a ton of momentum after blasting a short-handed Mississippi State team by a score of 31-0. Although quarterback Kamario Taylor was inactive for Mississippi State last weekend, LSU's shutout victory should re-instill some confidence in head coach Lane Kiffin's locker room following a tough road loss to Kentucky in Week 6. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt is off to a phenomenal start to his first season in Baton Rouge, already throwing for 1,785 yards with an 83.1 QBR — both of which rank 14th in all of college football. While Leavitt's 14 passing touchdowns have been quite impressive as well, the former Sun Devil has thrown a relatively concerning eight interceptions through the Tigers' first seven contests. Many deemed Kiffin's Tigers a definitive National Championship contender heading into the season, but dropping two SEC games before Week 8 could prove to be fatal for LSU. Saturday's game is a clear must-win spot for both teams, but even more so for LSU, which must face the likes of Alabama, Texas and Tennessee following its matchup versus Auburn. The keys to victory for LSU will be for Leavitt to minimize turnovers and to establish the run with sophomore tailback Dilin Jones. Jones is poised for a breakout performance, as I expect Auburn's defensive game plan to largely center around containing the Tigers' elite passing game. Given Auburn's road upset over then-No. 1 Georgia last weekend, Kiffin will undoubtedly be looking to make a statement in Week 8 before facing a gauntlet of a remaining SEC schedule. Auburn Tigers Betting Preview It has been a whirlwind of a campaign for Auburn thus far. In what really marked a new era for this program, first-year head coach Alex Golesh came in to take over the reins as Auburn's head coach following an abysmal three-year stretch under Hugh Freeze, who won just 15-of-34 games over that span. Golesh gained a great reputation as a sharp offensive-minded coach after a very successful stint as head coach at South Florida . Much of that can be attributed to the phenomenal play from dual-threat quarterback Byrum Brown , who followed Golesh to Auburn. The Tigers' first-year head coach has done a stellar job installing an explosive veer-and-shoot offensive scheme, which is a far more modern spread offense that uses extreme receiver splits and a fast tempo to stress defenses both horizontally and vertically. Despite Brown's move to the SEC leading to some subpar play early in the season, the Tigers' QB is finally starting to find his groove in the pocket, currently posting a top-35 QBR of 71.5. The former USF star has made much more of an impact on the ground, already racking up a whopping 460 rushing yards to go with five rushing touchdowns this season. His passing mechanics have improved substantially as well. In Auburn's spectacular upset victory in Athens last weekend, Brown threw for over 150 yards and a touchdown while also racking up 115 yards on the ground. He has now scored a rushing touchdown in five of the team's first six contests. To knock off the Tigers, Golesh's bunch will surely need another huge offensive performance from its superstar dual-threat quarterback. We're in for a spectacular SEC showdown on Saturday afternoon featuring two teams with everything to play for before they enter the heart of a remarkably difficult conference schedule. From a betting perspective, I favor taking a more unique approach to extract value from this game. The spread gives me slight cause for concern because it could be a potential letdown spot for Auburn following its biggest win of the season. For my primary handicap, I feel confident that both Tiger squads will score at least 20 points on Saturday afternoon, which is currently available at -117 at DraftKings . Pick: Both Teams to Score 20+ Points (-117)

Can the Auburn Tigers pull off another upset in Year 1 under coach Alex Golesh? Auburn pulled off the biggest upset of the college football season by defeating No. 1 Georgia this past Saturday in Athens. Now, it turns its attention to the LSU Tigers as a team with confidence that has proven it can beat anyone. Auburn enters this game as the underdog. Correspondingly, the ESPN matchup predictor gives Auburn a 28.8% chance to win. Auburn will need to play the type of game it did against Georgia. It will need to control the line of scrimmage and consistently run the football. Auburn outgained Georgia 192-113 on the ground. The LSU Tigers are No. 1 in the conference in run defense, allowing just 88.1 yards per game on the ground. However, the Bulldogs are No. 2 in that category, and Auburn had success with Byrum Brown and the running backs. The turnover battle will be key once again. Auburn forced three turnovers against Georgia and did not commit any. Going into that game, interceptions had been an issue for Brown with seven on the season. Auburn will be facing a quarterback in Sam Leavitt who has thrown eight interceptions this season. The Auburn defense will need to create opportunities for the offense to gain an upset victory. A big advantage for Auburn is it is at home. Both of LSU's losses were away from Baton Rouge: at Ole Miss and at Kentucky. The crowd at Jordan-Hare should be electric on Saturday after Week 7's upset win at Georgia. What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. away.blurb: However, LSU hasn't left a game unscathed this year. Princewill Umanmielen and Jackson Harris exited the game with injuries and didn't return. He and Jo Simmons have a massive test this coming week against Umanmielen, who was previously questionable after missing most of the game against Mississippi State with an upper-body injury. We'll see if the Auburn offensive line is ready to protect quarterback Byrum Brown against it. Stanton Ramil graded out as an 80 on the right edge against Georgia in the epic Deep South's Oldest Rivalry upset . The interior held up remarkably well, with Wilson Zierer and Kenneth McManus taking starter snaps. Brown and Jeremiah Cobb showed out against the Dawgs with their best outings of the season. Auburn's run game could have a symbiotic effect with the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd and keep the pressure on LSU's defense. The Ole Miss transfer Umanmielen immediately puts one of Golesh's recent big decisions to the test. Alex Golesh understands the challenge LSU is on the edge As Golesh said about LSU, "Those edges are real, like real real." Not only is Umanmielen a handful, but Tennessee transfer Jordan Ross is also elite. Ross had six tackles and a sack against State this past Saturday. Ross has three sacks this year, which ranks third behind defensive tackle Deuce Geralds's five and Umanmielen's eight. The group is even playing without Gabriel Reliford, who tore his ACL in the spring. The roster Lane Kiffin recruited has an embarrassment of riches in Baton Rouge. Auburn's run game has breakout chance against LSU Umanmielen isn't as renowned against the run. With that said, LSU's defense is better overall against the run than the pass. If you're looking for ways to nab an upset on Saturday and prove the Plains is haunted for favored opponents , controlling the clock is one of the most obvious. Brown is the ultimate wild card for Auburn. If he can keep LSU's defense guessing, opening up running lanes in the middle for Auburn when LSU's linebackers drop into coverage, perhaps Cobb, Omar Mabson, and the rest of the running backs could be difference-makers in a pivotal SEC clash.

Tennessee is coming off a massive win over Alabama . So naturally, South Carolina is favored over the Volunteers in Saturday's matchup in Columbia. The Gamecocks had a week to relish in their impressive road upset of Florida and rest up during their bye, while many are expecting a Vols letdown after such an emotional high and a field-storming last week. Week 8 bold predictions: Are BYU, Tennessee on upset alert? More: Week 8 schedule looks quiet. Here's where chaos could strike SEC letdowns have been popular this season: Ole Miss lost to Florida after beating LSU. Florida lost to Missouri after beating Ole Miss. Scott is doubtful and Miller is listed as questionable. There were no new injured Tennessee players listed on the initial SEC student-athlete availability report for the game against South Carolina. However, seven Tennessee players have already suffered season-ending injuries: starting left guard Wendell Moe ; starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). MacIntyre is 2-0 as a starter and completed 21-of-31 passes for 197 yards and an interception in Tennessee's 26-10 win over Alabama last week. Faizon Brandon, who won the starting QB job out of camp, dressed but did not play vs. the Crimson Tide. "MacIntyre … you see him continuing to get better each and every week," Shane Beamer said . "With his ability to run the offense, get rid of the ball when it's not there in the passing game, sit in the pocket, throw the ball downfield, but make good decisions and continue to play winning football. Against Florida, Stewart had his best performance of the season, with five tackles (four solo), two forced fumbles, one sack and one tackle for loss. It was only one game a few weeks ago in horrendous conditions, but the Gamecocks' 38-19 win over Florida showed one thing more than anything else – they're still trying. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. "Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?" said McElroy. "Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. "I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon." "Tennessee's defense is amazing," added McElroy. "They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks." Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: ‘More questions than answers’: Kansas State QB Avery Johnson’s return remains uncertain
away.blurb: He added that "it's not off the table" that Johnson could return at some point this season . Johnson appeared on the Wildcats' initial availability report on Wednesday, ahead of the Wildcats' Oct. 24 game in Tempe, Arizona. He was downgraded to doubtful Friday, then ruled out in the hours before the game against the Sun Devils . Fifth-year Jacob Knuth started in his place. "We're still trying to handle things," Klein told reporters. "Our medical staff and doctors are doing a great job of working through everything and making sure that we do it right." Saturday marked the first game Johnson has missed in his three seasons as the team's starter. The injury stems from the first quarter of the Wildcats' Oct. 17 win over Kansas when he fell to the turf after a long run. He missed one play before returning the next drive and playing the rest of the game without any noticeable issues. In his absence, Knuth completed 26 of 41 passes for 194 yards and a touchdown, and rushed for 19 yards and a score in his first career start. The Wildcats only rushed for 84 yards as a team. Johnson was on the sideline throughout the Wildcats' loss. When the defense was on the field, Johnson often helped Knuth. Unless he's back behind center, Johnson would likely have a similar role when the Wildcats travel to Colorado for a 1 p.m. CT game at Folsom Field in Boulder. "Again, there's more questions right now than answers," Klein said. "I think there's a lot just up in the air here in this next week or so to kind of see how things progress. "(He handled it) like a great teammate. He cares about winning; he cares about K-State. He and Jacob are dear, dear friends. He would do anything for this place, and to play and compete... it's just who he is." Wyatt D. Wheeler covers Kansas State athletics for the USA TODAY Network and Topeka Capital-Journal. away.headline: Kansas State Coach Collin Klein Gives Unusual Avery Johnson Injury Update
away.blurb: Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson missed Saturday’s 28-17 loss to Arizona State, and it doesn’t sound like the Wildcats have a firm timetable for when their star quarterback will return. Johnson surprisingly appeared on Kansas State’s injury report Wednesday as questionable before being downgraded to doubtful Friday and ultimately ruled out ahead of Saturday’s game. The exact nature of the injury has not been disclosed. Kansas State QB Avery Johnson Questionable for Big 12 Road Game at Arizona State Avery Johnson Injury: Collin Klein Gives Latest Update Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today Following the loss in Tempe, Kansas State head coach Collin Klein was asked about Johnson’s status and when he might be able to get back on the field. “There’s a few more questions than answers right now,” Klein said. “Still trying to handle things, and our medical staff and doctors are doing a great job of working through everything and making sure that we do it right.” That leaves Johnson’s status very much up in the air as Kansas State turns its attention toward next Saturday’s home game against Colorado. The injury appears to stem from Kansas State’s win over Kansas in the Sunflower Showdown. Johnson broke off a 59-yard run in the first quarter before going down awkwardly and leaving the game for one play. He returned on the following possession and finished the game, throwing for 209 yards and a touchdown while adding 132 rushing yards. Without Johnson against Arizona State, fifth-year senior Jacob Knuth made his first career start and finished 26-of-41 for 194 yards and one touchdown. Kansas State struggled to establish its running game, however, finishing with just 84 rushing yards in the loss. Klein praised Knuth afterward, but there’s little question that getting Johnson back would provide a major boost for a Kansas State team that has now fallen to 4-3. For now, though, there appears to be legitimate uncertainty surrounding exactly when that will happen. Kansas State returns home to face Colorado on Saturday, October 31. picks.headline: Three bold predictions for Virginia Tech vs Clemson
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech football has an opportunity to accomplish something it hasn’t done since 2007: defeat Clemson. The Hokies (5-2, 2-2 ACC) travel to Death Valley on Saturday for a 7 p.m. ET matchup against the Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) on ESPN , with bowl eligibility on the line for James Franklin’s squad. Virginia Tech enters the contest following a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech, while Clemson is coming off a 37-0 shutout of Charleston Southern. Despite the Tigers’ recent success, Clemson has struggled offensively throughout much of the season, potentially opening the door for Virginia Tech to snap its seven-game losing streak against the program. With that said, here are three predictions for Virginia Tech’s Saturday night showdown against Clemson. No. 1: Ethan Grunkemeyer throws for 300-plus yards and three touchdowns. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has established himself as one of the ACC’s more productive signal-callers, completing 167 of 229 passes for 1,984 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions through seven games. The Penn State transfer is coming off another solid performance against Georgia Tech, completing 15 of 22 passes for 250 yards and three touchdowns — though 215 of his 250 yards came before halftime. While Clemson’s defense has been respectable against opposing passing attacks, Grunkemeyer has demonstrated an ability to stretch the field with his receiving corps at his best, crossing the 300-yard mark twice. One player who could benefit is wide receiver Que’Sean Brown, who recorded a career-high 182 receiving yards against Georgia Tech last weekend. Clemson defensive coordinator Tom Allen’s familiarity with Franklin’s offensive system could complicate matters, but the Hokies have enough weapons to create explosive plays. I think Grunkemeyer surpasses 300 passing yards for the third time this season, throwing three touchdowns in the process. No. 2: Virginia Tech forces at least two Clemson turnovers. Clemson’s offensive struggles have been well-documented throughout the season, particularly through the air. The Tigers have thrown just two touchdown passes through six games, with freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds experiencing growing pains since assuming the starting role. Against Miami, Reynolds was sacked six times and threw a fourth-quarter interception that was returned for a touchdown. Clemson’s quarterbacks also combined for two interceptions against Charleston Southern last weekend. Virginia Tech’s defensive front has been one of the bright spots for the Hokies, particularly against opposing rushing attacks. The unit enters Saturday allowing just 87.4 rushing yards per game, ranking among the nation’s best. If Virginia Tech can limit Clemson’s ground game and force the Tigers into obvious passing situations, opportunities for takeaways should present themselves. The Hokies haven’t always capitalized on those opportunities this season, but Saturday could provide an opportunity to change that narrative. No. 3: Virginia Tech defeats Clemson for the first time since 2007 Perhaps the boldest prediction of the three is also the most consequential. Virginia Tech hasn’t defeated Clemson since a 41-23 victory in Blacksburg during the 2007 season, with the Tigers winning seven consecutive meetings since then. Dabo Swinney has never lost to the Hokies as Clemson’s head coach, going 6-0 against Virginia Tech — though it’s not the same Tigers that dominated the ACC in the 2010s. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, has demonstrated significant improvement under Franklin, even if close losses against Pitt and California have prevented the Hokies from entering Saturday with a better record. The Hokies’ previous five games have all been decided by 10 points or fewer, and another competitive contest seems likely. With Grunkemeyer leading the offense and Virginia Tech’s defensive front capable of disrupting Clemson’s inconsistent passing attack, the Hokies have an opportunity to escape Death Valley with their sixth victory. Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. Mandatory Credit: Brian Bishop-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Thomas Hughes Sat, October 24, 2026 at 4:26 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Virginia Tech football has an opportunity to accomplish two things Saturday night in Clemson, S.C., with a win: It'd secure bowl eligibility for the first time under head coach James Franklin and snap a nearly two-decade-long drought against Clemson . The Hokies (5-2, 2-2 ACC) travel to Memorial Stadium to face the Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC), with kickoff scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. Virginia Tech enters Saturday following a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech, snapping a two-game losing streak after consecutive defeats against Pittsburgh and California. Clemson, meanwhile, is coming off a 37-0 shutout of Charleston Southern, having won four of its previous five contests - though it opened the season with a 51-10 loss to then-No. 11 LSU. The Tigers have dominated in recent meetings, winning seven consecutive showdowns with the Hokies. Virginia Tech's last victory against Clemson came in 2007, when the Hokies defeated the Tigers 41-23 in Blacksburg. However, Saturday's matchup presents an intriguing opportunity for Virginia Tech, particularly given the contrasting production from the two programs' quarterbacks. Virginia Tech's offense The Hokies' offensive improvement has been one of the defining developments of Franklin's first season, with quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer leading the charge. Through seven games, Grunkemeyer has completed 167 of 229 passes (72.9%) for 1,984 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions, averaging 8.7 yards per attempt. The Penn State transfer has developed a particularly strong connection with Duke transfer Que'Sean Brown, who leads Virginia Tech with 46 receptions for 616 yards and three touchdowns. Brown is coming off his most productive performance of the season, recording six receptions for a career-high 182 yards and a touchdown against Georgia Tech - a 60-yard score on the second play of Virginia Tech's first drive. The Hokies have also received considerable production from sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr., who has recorded 613 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 103 carries, averaging 5.95 yards per attempt. Overton's contributions extend beyond the ground game - he's added 22 receptions for 219 yards and two touchdowns. That versatility could prove important against a Clemson defense featuring several talented playmakers, including defensive end Will Heldt and linebackers Sammy Brown and Jeremiah Alexander. Clemson's offense While Virginia Tech has experienced considerable offensive success, Clemson has struggled to establish consistency, particularly at quarterback. True freshman Tait Reynolds has assumed starting responsibilities following Christopher Vizzina's elbow injury earlier this season. Through six games, Reynolds has thrown for 943 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. His struggles have been particularly noticeable on deep passes, completing just two of 21 attempts traveling at least 20 yards downfield. Clemson has recorded just two passing touchdowns this season, a significant departure from the offensive production traditionally associated with Dabo Swinney's program. However, the Tigers have found success through sophomore running back Gideon Davidson. Davidson leads Clemson with 430 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 79 carries, averaging 5.4 yards per attempt. His most productive performance came against California, when he rushed for 159 yards and two touchdowns. Wide receiver Bryant Wesco Jr. leads Clemson with 29 receptions for 340 yards, while T.J. Moore has contributed 27 catches for 244 yards and one touchdown. Perhaps Virginia Tech's biggest advantage comes along the defensive line, where senior Aycen Stevens has emerged as one of the ACC's premier pass rushers. Stevens enters Saturday with 10.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks, including 1.5 sacks and 2.5 tackles for loss against Georgia Tech. That could spell trouble for Clemson, which has surrendered 17 sacks through six games. However, the Tigers possess considerable defensive talent of their own. Safety Corey Myrick leads Clemson with 44 tackles, while Sammy Brown has recorded 41. Cornerback Elliot Washington II has also registered three interceptions. Another important factor will be Virginia Tech's ability to finish drives. The Hokies have struggled with turnovers and offensive inconsistency at times, particularly in their losses to Pitt and California. Against a Clemson defense capable of creating negative plays, protecting Grunkemeyer and avoiding costly penalties could determine whether Virginia Tech leaves Death Valley victorious. Virginia Tech has the more productive quarterback and several offensive weapons capable of creating explosive plays. However, Clemson's defensive talent and home-field advantage make this a difficult matchup. If Grunkemeyer protects the football and the Hokies contain Davidson, Virginia Tech has a legitimate opportunity to secure its sixth victory. For Clemson, this is a chance to begin building a stronger second-half résumé and avoid another setback in the ACC race. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images C_Craft Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:41 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nitty Gritty Time Has Arrived for 2026 Greetings once again STS readers! Dabo Swinney always says each week is the "biggest game of the year" but even he has conceded that some games have more juice than others. This would have to be considered one of those games. While it isn't on the scale of a top-ten matchup, or even what it might have been back in 2011 when Clemson traveled to face VT or when they saw the Hokies again in the ACC title game, it is a vital tipping point for both teams looking to regain relevance. The winner of this game stays firmly in the hunt for a chance to go to Charlotte. Reaching 10 wins would be a huge accomplishment for this year's Tigers, and despite the two lopsided losses, it would be a step back up after 2025's major letdown. Before we get to the matchup, here is my good, bad, and ugly from last week's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern. The Good: Clemson's defense was lights out beyond a few moments during CSU's first drive when their scripted plays found some success ahead of a missed FG attempt. I was most encouraged by how well the depth performed, particularly in the secondary, as they got subbed more and more into the game. The upgrade in secondary execution across the board cannot be understated after last year's debacles. Clemson's special teams continues to shine week in and week out. I said Chris Johnson, Jr. was on the verge of scoring a kickoff return and nearly did it on his one opportunity. Nolan Hauser continues to look like an NFL starter and the coverage team produced a turnover for a touchdown for loyal Tiger Kylon Griffin. The Bad: Red zone offense wasn't ugly because the Tigers did punch in touchdown runs from CJJ and Gideon Davidson, but obviously there were more missed chances and bad penalties that continue to haunt this year's offense inside the 20 yard line. 37 points easily could have been 57 points or more considering the defensive and special teams dominance. The Ugly: Clemson's downfield passing attack gets the nod for the ugly. Especially when Tait Reynolds delivered plenty of throws that were there for big-money WRs TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco. Reynolds also apparently missed Moore running wide open on a post at least once, but lack of WR production and TDs were not on Chad Morris's play calls. He's getting 1 on 1 scenarios for the outside guys and they need to pay those off the way they are being paid to do. Clemson can't afford to miss those in these next stretch of games. Now that we are done with that, on to the 5-2 Hokies. Clemson Offense vs. VT Defense: There are several reasons to have some apprehension as a Clemson fan looking at this game. Clemson's running attack has proven to be much further along than the downfield passing game. It isn't a coincidence that Clemson has run the ball effectively in the 4 wins and failed miserably to do so in the 2 losses. Clemson's passing attack has yet to prove it can go win if it has to and VT's defense has been good against the run so far this season. They have given up a lot of passing yards, however, but can Reynolds and the offense deliver enough to exploit that apparent weakness? Any DC with a functional brain is going to try to force Reynolds to throw to win, which will mean loading up on the run and sending pressures regularly. Clemson fans are going to get another real sign if the OL has gotten its act together more with the new (and reportedly best) group of five guys out there together. VT is a pressure defense and looks to force the issue which has helped them rack up good sack and TFL numbers as well as effective run defense, but likewise has opened them up to getting burned on explosives (especially in the passing game). Clemson desperately needs to hit on the explosive play chances that are going to be there and, of course, limit VT's ability to get them behind the chains. Dabo has harped on the team not winning the turnover margin in games this season. Clemson is certainly due to do that, but it starts with the offense not turning it over. Clemson ended up throwing the ball 44 times in the Miami game, and that number needs to be between 25-30 this week I think if Clemson is going to win. This team is not equipped to play shootout football right now, and VT is much more capable of that and has had those types of games already. Reynolds has cut down on putting the ball in jeopardy, and a big part of that is having better pass protection to begin with, but he's been a little loose with the ball as a runner. Reynolds managed to avoid a bad turnover last week when he pounced on his own fumble, but the margin of error is not big in any of these remaining games to overcome putting the ball on the ground. I discussed the Moore/Wesco duo earlier, but it is imperative one or both deliver and win their matchups that VT is going to present them with in order to try to force Clemson away from the running game. I liked a lot of the concepts Morris showed to get the ball to the outside guys in various ways, including using bootlegs with Wesco coming across where you traditionally use a tight end. TJ Moore has been best on the slant in the RPO game, but he needs to win more of the outside fade situations that he has not been nearly as good with this season. Gordon Sellars is out with a concussion, and that eliminates at least one of the plan B options that Chad Morris very thinly veiled that he desired to have to push Moore when he has his press conference on Wednesday. Clemson needs the 2024 Texas game or 2025 SMU game version of TJ Moore on Saturday night. VT is similar in some ways to Miami defensively in that their front is stronger than their secondary. Clemson was unable to exploit Miami enough outside to offset being beaten at the point of attack that night. Clemson still needs to get at least 100 net yards rushing to keep that part of the offense relevant. The running back room is plenty good enough to deliver with Jay Haynes now back with Davidson and Johnson. They need to be given ample chances to deliver in this game. Clemson Defense vs. VT Offense : Clemson's defense is certainly ahead of the offense in the growth department. Part of this is because the big money guys on this side of the ball are playing like they are big money guys more consistently. This will be a real test considering VT has at least one playmaker at WR, RB, and TE to go with an NFL prospect at QB. Clemson has to make sure that VT can't get its running game going with Jeffrey Overton because he can hurt you badly if you let him get loose. BC found this out in nasty weather when Overton cooked them for 209 yards. Pittsburgh escaped with a win over the Hokies despite giving up nearly 500 yards of offense and 33 points, but one big reason was VT couldn't run the ball and passing more led to more turnovers. Ethan Grunkemeyer is a good player as Clemson fans saw last year when he handled the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl, but you still want him having to attack the strength of Clemson's back end versus having the balance of the running game to set things up and protect him. I worry the most about VT using Overton in the screen game and their dynamic tight end Luke Reynolds because those guys will match up with Clemson's nickel, safeties, or linebackers and not Ashton Hampton or Elliot Washington. It will be vital to make Grunkemeyer hold the ball so the rush can get there and get hands in the passing lanes on VT's RPO game. VT can be turned over, but that depends a lot on getting them into more obvious passing scenarios and heating Grunkemeyer up. Penn State was able to manage enough of a run game and largely keep Clemson's depleted defensive front from bothering him last year in the bowl game. He can really hurt you if you let him stand there and get through his reads. Clemson isn't going to keep VT under 100 yards and shut them out like they did CSU unless they deliver in some crazy way that far surpasses expectations. VT has too much talent to not have some success, but Clemson's ability to turn them over and force field goal attempts will be massive. Clemson can win a game in the 20s, but allowing VT to get to 30 or more probably means a big fat L for the Tigers on Saturday night. Getting VT at home helps for sure because they have been way better in Lane Stadium than on the road, such as when they allowed a depleted California squad to take them down. VT has been a fast-starting team, which usually means they are good at their opening 12-15 play script, so Clemson needs to be locked in right away on defense. Special Teams: Most fans who have been around since the 2000s know how much special teams helped Frank Beamer elevate VT to a top 20 program. It certainly was a major factor when Clemson lost a critical game with the Hokies back in 2007. Ironically, now the Tigers have the differential special teams play heading into this matchup thanks to outstanding work across the board under Rich Bisaccia. Returns look dangerous, coverage has been largely terrific, and Nolan Hauser has to be among the frontrunners for the Lou Groza Award. This game is pretty close on paper for sure, so this phase could be the difference. None of Clemson's games has featured a special teams fake this season, so Clemson has to be alert. Fortunately there hasn't really been any reason for Clemson to try to get fancy on returns or on kicks. The closest thing was Nolan Hauser's pooch punt at California that paid off with a roughing penalty, but that is exactly why you run something like that on a defense that isn't prepped to defend a punt. Overall: There is a lot about this 2026 team that reminds me of the 2021 team. I ended up really liking that 21 team mainly because they showed real toughness to overcome the obvious warts and squeezed 10 wins out of a team that easily could have only won 7. That isn't what you want year in and year out as a fan, especially when "Best is the Standard" is written in your facility, but this team has always been more about getting back to being tough. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V."
