away.blurb: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out Skip to main content About One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. home.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

home.headline: Latest Injury Report Lists Thomas Williams, Others OUT vs. Clemson
home.blurb: The latest injury report for Virginia Tech vs. Clemson lists several Hokies OUT for tonight’s game. There was optimism that Virginia Tech cornerback Thomas Williams would suit up on Saturday after being reported as a full participant on Wednesday during the open media portion of practice, but the latest injury report submitted to the ACC has downgraded Williams to OUT today when the Hokies face Clemson. Williams was injured while making a tackle during Saturday's win over Georgia Tech a week ago. "I did think he was playing well on Saturday," head coach James Franklin said after practice this week of Williams. "So, being able to have him back and building confidence each week is a big one for us, because he can run and, as you guys know, this Clemson roster is talented and we've got to make sure that all of the guys that we have that have horsepower are available. He's one of our most explosive, fastest guys on the team." Virginia Tech and Clemson will kick off tonight at 7:00 PM EST on ESPN. home.headline: DT Vic Burley added to injury report for Clemson vs Virginia Tech
home.blurb: Burley, a senior, was listed as questionable again after being added Oct. 22. He was not listed on the initial report Oct. 21. Burley has played in four games after missing the first two because of a suspension. He got his first tackle, a sack, in Week 7 vs Georgia Southern. Clemson wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is listed as out. Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said that Sellars has a concussion and is going through concussion protocol. He's made three catches for 8 yards in a backup role. Defensive tackle Devarrick Woods and running back Jarvis Green don't appear on the injury report for Clemson. Swinney has said that he expects both players to return from injury against Virginia Tech. Vizzina was removed from the Tigers' injury report against California on Sept. 25 ahead of kickoff that night and hasn't appeared once since. However, Vizzina hasn't fully recovered, and he was only available for emergencies against Miami and Charleston Southern. The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) square off with Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2) at home on Oct. 24 (7 p.m., ESPN). Christopher Vizzina injury update Swinney said backup quarterback Christopher Vizzina is having his "best week by far" of the season and that he's 90% healthy. Vizzina has been recovering from a small fracture in his left elbow after originally injuring it against Georgia Southern on Sept. 12. Swinney said after the Charleston Southern game that he wouldn't have had an issue with playing Vizzina against the Buccaneers, but that Vizzina told him he wasn't ready and that Brock Bradley should enter instead. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out
home.blurb: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out Skip to main content About One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball Coming off a 34-24 victory at home over Georgia Tech last Saturday, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road for the first of two road games sandwiched around their bye week on Oct. 31 in Death Valley in South Carolina against Clemson. The Hokies will be looking to become bowl-eligible with a win after winning five of their first seven games, while the Tigers come in at 4-2 in a battle in primetime on ESPN between a pair of two-loss ACC teams in late October. NEW AVAILABILITY REPORT Cam Chadwick is off the report for the Hokies, while DT Vic Burley has been added for Clemson. pic.twitter.com/yEN9gsML54 Freshman Benjamin Eziuka played nearly 50 snaps against the Yellow Jackets last weekend and will be ready to go this weekend if Cunningham can't go again. It'll be a tough environment for Eziuka to play at Clemson, but Franklin doesn't appear to be nervous about putting him in. "He's dense; he's powerful in the weight room, and he's super trustworthy," Franklin said at his Wednesday media availability . "Obviously, everybody uses that quote: 'Do your job.' He's that guy. You know what you're going to get from him every single day." Virginia Tech announces Commonwealth Clash sellout This weekend's ACC slate begins on Friday

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with the unique culture of Ole Miss all around him. His uncle, Eli Manning, had his jersey retired in Oxford, as was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has rediscovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Follow along for LIVE updates, highlights and analysis as Ole Miss takes on Texas. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. The Longhorns need to find answers on offense and need to hold onto leads in the second half. That'll be easier said than done with star defensive end Colin Simmons being listed as doubtful for Saturday against a dynamic offense in No. 7 Ole Miss. Here is how the Texas Longhorns On SI staff believes the matchup will play out. Matt Galatzan This is pretty simple from my perspective. If Texas puts the same team on the field that it has for the last four weeks, this one is not going to be close. Trinidad Chambliss is the best quarterback in the country. Kewan Lacy - when healthy - might be the best running back in the country. But where Ole Miss has needed to change, and has changed it seems, is on the defensive side of the ball. Can Texas do the same on the offensive side of the ball in six days? I'm not so sure about that. picks.blurb: College GameDay Makes Official Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Texas Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels will travel to Austin, Texas, tonight to take on the No. 19 Texas Longhorns in a ranked conference matchup with major College Football Playoff implications. Ole Miss will be looking for its third straight win following victories against Vanderbilt and No. 22 Missouri. Texas will be looking to bounce back after two consecutive losses against Oklahoma and No. 20 Florida. Texas will be without key players in edge rusher Colin Simmons and running back Hollywood Smothers. The team may also be making a change at quarterback , as backup KJ Lacey Jr. has taken more first-team reps from Arch Manning than normal in practice this week. ESPN's College GameDay was in Salt Lake City, Utah, this morning to preview No. 10 Utah vs. No. 14 Houston, but still found time to have Desmond Howard, Rece Davis, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban, Kirk Herbstreit and guest picker Dalton Kincaid make picks for Ole Miss vs. Texas. Here are the picks: Mississippi Rebels safety Joenel Aguero celebrates with safeties Nick Cull and Sharif Denson after a defensive stop during the second half at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Desmond Howard: Ole Miss Desmond Howard: Ole Miss The Michigan alumni and former Heisman Trophy winner isn't trusting Texas' defense without Colin Simmons. "Defensively, without Colin Simmons, I don't see how they can stop Trinidad Chambliss. I'm going with Ole Miss," Howard said. Nick Saban: Texas Both Texas' and Ole Miss' head coaches spent time on Nick Saban's staff at Alabama. In a game with playoff implications, Saban backed Texas' Steve Sarkisian to have his team bounce back. "Texas, with their back against the wall, they're going to respond the right way. I'm going with Texas," Saban said. Pat McAfee: Ole Miss McAfee compared this game to a coin flip, saying he wants to pick both teams, but is maintaining faith in Ole Miss' star quarterback. "I'm gonna go with Trinidad Chambliss getting a huge win down in Austin," McAfee said. Dalton Kincaid: Ole Miss The former Utah Ute and current Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid followed the trend and put his faith in Trinidad Chambliss. "I'm also taking Ole Miss here," Kincaid said. "I think Trinidad Chambliss is one of the, if not the best, quarterbacks in college football, so I believe they go in there and take down Texas." Three of the four pickers selected Ole Miss. The teams will kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT tonight to see if they chose correctly. For the first time in over a decade, Texas and Ole Miss meet today at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The lines on Kalshi have the Longhorns favored by 3.5 at home with the total at 53.5, and despite back-to-back losses, my Ole Miss vs. Texas prediction and college football picks project Arch Manning to pull off a win against his namesake's alma mater. For the rest of today's slate, see our Week 8 college football top picks and Brad Powers' Week 8 predictions . TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas tonight? Pick: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . While the Longhorns have lost two straight, they still have the clear defensive advantage, even with Colin Simmons unlikely to play. The Texas defense ranks sixth nationally in available yards percentage (31.2%) and 14th in havoc rate (20%). Check the college football injury report for Simmons' status before kickoff. Meanwhile, the Ole Miss defense struggled in ranked matchups away from home, allowing 90 points across two games. It's a big ask for Trinidad Chambliss to make up for his own defense again against one of the top defenses in the country. Chambliss is coming off arguably his worst game of the season, too (80.4 QBR, 65.7% adjusted completion percentage vs. Missouri ). For more spread plays, see our college football Week 8 picks against the spread . Ole Miss vs Texas Over/Under pick: Over 53.5 While Texas' defensive advantage should make the difference in a Longhorns win, I'm expecting enough points to be scored for the Over to hit at 54.5 or better . The Ole Miss defense ranks 65th nationally in success rate (43.5%) and 89th in net EPA per drive, while allowing the most yards per game in the SEC (390). It's been at its worst away from home, allowing 35.6 points per game outside Oxford , helping the Over in all three of those games. Ole Miss vs Texas prop: Texas team total Over 27.5 While Pete Golding is a defensive coach, his team's defense has been sporadic at best this season. Ole Miss' defense ranks outside the top 75 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and early-down EPA per play. It's really struggled away from Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, allowing 38+ points and over 460 yards in two of its three games away from home . The biggest issue for Ole Miss is stopping the run. The Rebels have allowed the most rushing yards per game in the SEC (153.5). That should help Steve Sarkisian take pressure off Manning by leaning on his running backs. While Chambliss is my midseason first-team All-American QB, Ole Miss can't keep getting away with relying on him to carry it to wins, and allowing 29.2 points per game against ranked teams will catch up to the Rebels. Without Simmons, this Texas defense will take a step back, but not a big enough step for Ole Miss to light it up and make up for its own defensive woes. Games away from home have been unkind to the Rebels, especially their defense, and I think Manning, Sarkisian, and the Longhorns offense will rise to the occasion to take advantage. A true must-win game is one that staves off elimination. Well, that's essentially what the Longhorns face Saturday night when Texas hosts the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium. Just three weeks ago, the Longhorns were the No. 1 team in the nation. Now Texas is fighting for its College Football Playoff life. Steve Sarkisian has gone from the savior of the program to the hottest seat in America. And Arch Manning has gone from superstar to punchline. It has all gone so wrong so quickly. But Mississippi provides an opportunity for the entire Longhorns football program to put the past two weeks behind it and become the contender they're supposed to be ... on paper at least. We discussed after the Ohio State game that this Longhorns team might only play all-out and all-in when pushed the the brink . This is the brink. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas is staring down what seems to be a must-win vs. Ole Miss . The offense has given little reason for confidence and the defense, likely without Colin Simmons, has to contain one of the best QBs in the country. For Texas to end their losing streak streak, they'll need their most complete performance of the season. It's difficult for me to see them mustering that, especially against Chambliss, Lacy and the Rebels offensive attack. Could Texas rise from the ashes like a pheonix and play like the contender everyone thought the were? Will UT figure out enough of its issues to play well and beat a playoff-calibre team in Ole Miss? Or will the entire Steve Sarkisian/Arch Manning era come crashing down on the DKR turf. The smart money is on the later. Texas and Manning has looked completely lost for two weeks. Desperation can be a great motivator. One odd meltdown of a loss to Oklahoma, and a way-too-tight loss to Florida later – both games were 27-24 – and now there's no more room to make a mistake. Yes, the College Football Playoff can do whatever it wants, but it has yet to take an at-large team with more than two losses that didn't play in a conference championship. 2025 Texas went 9-3 and didn't get in. away.headline: What Kewan Lacy shoulder injury that won't go away means for Ole Miss after Texas loss
away.blurb: Lacy exited in the third quarter with an injury. He was tackled by multiple Longhorn defenders on his 16th rushing attempt of the night and fell hard on his left shoulder . He was helped to the sideline and transported on a cart. He did not return to the game. Lacy entered the game against the Longhorns without being on the injury report, but he has been playing through an injury to his left shoulder since the beginning of the season. He also picked up a lower-body injury on Oct. 17 at Vanderbilt. Lacy was able to return to that game. Makhi Frazier handled most of the carries when Lacy was out. Frazier rushed for 47 yards six carries, which was highlighted by a 34-yard run. "You ain't getting any more 'my bads,'" Golding said. "That's what we said in the locker room. You ain't getting any days off anymore. That's over. So it's not easy week-in-and-week-out, but we've got the right group. The right type of guys. Good players. So we're going to go to work and see what happens." AUSTIN, TX — Ole Miss football was close to delivering on coach Pete Golding's parting words of encouragement to Kewan Lacy , but fell just short. No. 18 Texas beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 on Oct. 24 at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. The Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) mounted a 21-point comeback to tie the game but couldn't get in the end zone again vs Texas (5-2, 2-2). "I told him I love him, and keep his head up," Golding said. "I told him we're going to come back and we're going to win this thing." Golding did not have a definitive update about Lacy when asked at his postgame press conference, but indicated the injury was to his left shoulder. "I've not got an update on that," Golding said. "Obviously I was on the field with him. He was in a lot of pain. Same shoulder. Hoping we get an update soon." Kewan Lacy has battled injuries all season Lacy has been one of the top running backs in the nation since he burst onto the scene in 2025. He rushed for 1,567 yards and a school-record 24 touchdowns last season. This season he has 388 yards and five touchdowns. He is projected as a potential first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Despite Lacy's game-changing ability, his backup had the more efficient rushing statistics against the Longhorns. Lacy had rushed 16 times for 36 yards against Texas. It was a homecoming game for him. He grew up in Lancaster, Texas, and dreamed of signing with the Longhorns as a kid. Ole Miss has no open dates for the rest of the season, and will host Auburn on Oct. 31 (11:45 a.m.) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. With or without Lacy, the margin of error has tightened for the Rebels to reach the College Football Playoff. No three-loss team has made the CFP without making its conference championship. home.blurb: FINAL Ole Miss vs. Texas Injury Report: Brycen Sanders Cleared, Terez Davis a Game-Time Decision ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss will have its starting center in Austin. Brycen Sanders , who was listed as probable on Friday, is off the SEC's final game-day availability report, released at 5 p.m. CT, clearing him for tonight's game against No. 19 Texas. Left tackle Terez Davis , who was questionable all week, is now listed as a game-time decision. The eight Rebels ruled out on Friday remain out. For Texas, defensive back Kobe Black was added as a game-time decision. Offensive lineman Jackson Christian and running back Derrek Cooper are both off the report. Edge rushers Colin Simmons and Richard Wesley , running back Hollywood Smothers , wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman remain out. Off the report: OL Brycen Sanders, who was probable on Friday. Status change: OL Terez Davis, from questionable to game-time decision. No change: All eight players listed as out on Friday remain out. Added: DB Kobe Black, listed as a game-time decision. Off the report: OL Jackson Christian, who was questionable on Friday, and RB Derrek Cooper, who was probable. Sanders left last week's win over Missouri, and Patrick Kutas slid from right guard to center to finish the game. Black's status adds a question to the Texas secondary against a Rebel passing attack that averages 290.7 yards per game. home.headline: What Kewan Lacy shoulder injury that won't go away means for Ole Miss after Texas loss
home.blurb: Lacy exited in the third quarter with an injury. He was tackled by multiple Longhorn defenders on his 16th rushing attempt of the night and fell hard on his left shoulder . He was helped to the sideline and transported on a cart. He did not return to the game. Lacy entered the game against the Longhorns without being on the injury report, but he has been playing through an injury to his left shoulder since the beginning of the season. He also picked up a lower-body injury on Oct. 17 at Vanderbilt. Lacy was able to return to that game. Makhi Frazier handled most of the carries when Lacy was out. Frazier rushed for 47 yards six carries, which was highlighted by a 34-yard run. "You ain't getting any more 'my bads,'" Golding said. "That's what we said in the locker room. You ain't getting any days off anymore. That's over. So it's not easy week-in-and-week-out, but we've got the right group. The right type of guys. Good players. So we're going to go to work and see what happens." AUSTIN, TX — Ole Miss football was close to delivering on coach Pete Golding's parting words of encouragement to Kewan Lacy , but fell just short. No. 18 Texas beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 on Oct. 24 at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. The Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) mounted a 21-point comeback to tie the game but couldn't get in the end zone again vs Texas (5-2, 2-2). "I told him I love him, and keep his head up," Golding said. "I told him we're going to come back and we're going to win this thing." Golding did not have a definitive update about Lacy when asked at his postgame press conference, but indicated the injury was to his left shoulder. "I've not got an update on that," Golding said. "Obviously I was on the field with him. He was in a lot of pain. Same shoulder. Hoping we get an update soon." Kewan Lacy has battled injuries all season Lacy has been one of the top running backs in the nation since he burst onto the scene in 2025. He rushed for 1,567 yards and a school-record 24 touchdowns last season. This season he has 388 yards and five touchdowns. He is projected as a potential first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Despite Lacy's game-changing ability, his backup had the more efficient rushing statistics against the Longhorns. Lacy had rushed 16 times for 36 yards against Texas. It was a homecoming game for him. He grew up in Lancaster, Texas, and dreamed of signing with the Longhorns as a kid. Ole Miss has no open dates for the rest of the season, and will host Auburn on Oct. 31 (11:45 a.m.) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. With or without Lacy, the margin of error has tightened for the Rebels to reach the College Football Playoff. No three-loss team has made the CFP without making its conference championship. We previewed Vanderbilt's offense and defense as they are in a massive transition year. We also list our X factors for the game on both sides of the football. After laying out Kentucky 's path to victory in this game, I will now give my final thoughts and prediction. Kentucky is playing a night game in front of a sold out Kroger Field, and this will be true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis' first road SEC night game. The city is buzzing watching year one of Will Stein and the big blue nation will certainly play a factor in this football game. Kentucky's coaching staff is ensuring this team does not overlook the Commodores, as they are reminding them the beatdown they suffered last season in Nashville and the incident of Vanderbilt players disrespecting the UK logo at midfield last time they were in Lexington. There are plenty of impact players for the Wildcats that remember the whooping they took last season, so I do not think Kentucky will sleep walk their way into the bye week. As we stated when we laid out Kentucky's path to victory, this game is a massive advantage for the Wildcats on the line of scrimmage. Kentucky's offensive line has been incredible this season, and I expect them to get a ton of movement in the running game as well as keeping quarterback Kenny Minchey clean in the pocket. On the other side of the football, Kentucky's defensive line should dominate this Vanderbilt offensive line. Jared Curtis will be facing pressure, but the key for the Wildcats is to get him on the ground and not let him extend plays by erasing sack opportunities. Another key area is always the turnover margin, and Kentucky is one of the best teams in the nation at winning the turnover margin consistently. Statistically, Kentucky ranks third in FBS with a +11 turnover margin, trailing only New Mexico and Notre Dame. This is a large advantage in Kentucky's favor, as Curtis is a true freshman and already has multiple interceptions and fumbles on the season. If Kentucky can continue to win the turnover battle as they have all season, this game has blowout potential. Kentucky's offense has yet to put it all together, we saw them at their best on the road at Texas A&M in a dominant third quarter performance. This could be the game where it clicks for four quarters for this offense. Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in success rate and explosive play rate combined. Vanderbilt is dead last in the conference in success rate allowed and they rank bottom five in the SEC in explosive play rate allowed. This is a huge opportunity for the Wildcats to put on an offensive showcase against an SEC team to go into the bye week on a high note. This game is monumental for Kentucky, and we have seen SEC teams struggle the game before their bye week this season. Kentucky has to put together a great game to go into a bye week where they could be a top ten team in the country the next time they take the field if they can get this win. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen over that bye week and if the Wildcats take care of business, they will be on the graphic. A win here could set up a November to remember for the Wildcats where everything is on the table from SEC Championship to College Football Playoff talks. Prediction: Kentucky 42, Vanderbilt 17 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Vanderbilt: Final Thoughts & Prediction

Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. picks.headline: How No. 12 Kentucky football and Vanderbilt match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey completed 21 of 28 passes for 158 yards and two touchdowns in the Wildcats’ 21-13 win at Oklahoma last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound transfer from Notre Dame has been a paragon of efficiency so far as a Wildcat. On the season, Minchey has completed 68.4% of his throws for 1,551 yards with 13 touchdowns vs. one interception . • Vanderbilt true freshman Jared Curtis is a player UK coach Will Stein sought to recruit while serving as Oregon offensive coordinator. “He’s very young,” Stein said of Curtis, “but in terms of the tangibles of the position, being able to throw it, arm talent, running strength, he is a prototype first-round-type talent.” A homegrown, 6-3, 230-pound Nashville product, Curtis is completing 62.7% of his throws for 1,242 yards and six touchdowns. Ball security has been an issue for the freshman QB, who has thrown seven interceptions and lost two fumbles. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky leading rusher CJ Baxter (484 yards, 5.6 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) sat out last week’s victory at Oklahoma with an undisclosed injury. In Baxter’s absence, third-year player Jason Patterson led UK with 38 yards on 12 carries vs. the Sooners. Former Oklahoma back Jovantae Barnes carried five times for 16 yards last week vs. his former team. • Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea deploys a two-man running back rotation. Senior Sedrick Alexander has run for 270 yards and five touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards a rush. The 5-9, 207-pound product of Austin, Texas, has also caught 11 passes for 94 yards and a score. Senior Makhilyn Young has rushed for 232 yards and two TDs and is averaging 4.2 yards a carry. A 5-10, 210-pound product of Midland, Texas, Young has caught 10 passes for 76 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby was named a Midseason Freshman All-American by On3 Sports this week. The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, leads UK with 34 catches and 436 receiving yards and is tied for the team lead with three touchdown receptions. Senior Nic Anderson made an acrobatic, juggling catch against Oklahoma — the team for whom he played as a freshman. Over the past three games, the 6-4, 205-pound Atlanta product has caught 13 passes. On the season, Anderson has 17 catches for 197 yards and a TD. • Vanderbilt senior Junior Sherrill is fourth in the SEC in receptions with 41. A 5-11, 200-pound Nashville product, Sherrill has 628 receiving yards and has caught four touchdown passes. In Vandy’s 45-17 strafing of UK last season, Sherrill caught eight passes for 115 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is putting together an All-SEC-caliber season. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School caught five passes for 38 yards and two touchdowns in last week’s win at Oklahoma. On the season, Rodriguez has 33 catches for 257 yards and three TDs. • A transfer from East Carolina who began his college career at Ole Miss, Vanderbilt’s Jayvontay Conner has 13 catches for 146 yards. Cole Spence has six receptions for 72 yards. In last season’s blowout of UK, Spence caught three passes for 48 yards. Offensive line • Kentucky left offensive tackle Lance Heard was named a First Team Mid-Season All-American this week by On3 Sports. A 6-6, 325-pound product of Bonita, Louisiana, Heard was recently ranked the 29th-best prospect for the 2027 NFL draft by CBSSports.com. • Vanderbilt “quick guard” Cade McConnell is the only returning starter along the offensive front from last season’s 10-3 team. A 6-5, 323-pound product of Choctaw, Oklahoma, McConnell began his college career at Minnesota. Center Lyndon Cooper logged 25 career starts at Pittsburgh and was considered a portal-recruiting coup for Vandy. Advantage: Kentucky Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace and tackle Tavion Gadson were disruptive forces for UK late in the win at Oklahoma. Humphrey-Grace, a 6-4, 271-pound senior from Cincinnati, was credited with 1.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries vs. the Sooners. It was Humphrey-Grace deflecting the ball off the throwing hand of Oklahoma QB John Mateer that set up the Ty Bryant interception that was the turning point in the game. Gadson, a 6-5, 303-pound junior from Savannah, Georgia, made eight tackles, 1.5 sacks and broke up a pass. “Those guys are really good players,” Will Stein said of Gadson and Humphrey-Grace. • At 6-7, 305 pounds, Vanderbilt tackle Issa Ouattara is an impactful presence in the interior of the Commodores’ defensive front. A product of Cologne, Germany, Ouattara has two sacks and three QB hurries so far in 2026. Edge Miles Capers leads Vandy with six tackles for loss and has two sacks, an interception and the forced fumble that set up Vanderbilt’s game-winning touchdown on the final play of a 35-31 victory over North Carolina State. • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey made a game-high 15 tackles at Oklahoma. WLB Bo Barnes was not far behind with 10 stops. It has been a season of starts and stops for fifth-year player Alex Afari . The 6-2, 227-pound Cincinnati product is a member of the high school class of 2022 that the NCAA has attempted to exclude from the new 5-for-5 eligibility model. Afari was eligible for UK’s first four games due to a ruling in Jefferson County Circuit Court. However, the NCAA won on appeal at the Kentucky Court of Appeals, making Afari ineligible for the South Carolina and LSU games. A subsequent ruling by the Jefferson County Circuit Court last week restored Afari’s eligibility prior to the Oklahoma contest. The legal back-and-forth “is frustrating for him and for us,” Will Stein said. “We just got to roll with the punches a little bit. It’s out of our control. It’s out of his control at the end of the day, and he’s responded appropriately.” • Vanderbilt WLB Nick Rinaldi is a stat stuffer. A 6-3, 240-pound product of Dover, Massachusetts, Rinaldi has made 42 tackles, 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks and has hurried the quarterback four times and broken up passes four times. MLB Bryan Longwell is second on the team with 50 tackles. Longwell had a TFL in Vandy’s rout of UK last season. Advantage : Vanderbilt Defensive backs • Kentucky senior safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each had two interceptions in the win over Oklahoma. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound transfer from Florida, foiled a Sooners’ fake field goal with an interception in the end zone and later returned a pick of John Mateer 41 yards for the game’s final touchdown. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Frederick Douglass High School alumnus, set up Kentucky’s go-ahead TD with a 42-yard interception return, then sealed the Wildcats’ victory with a pick with 21 seconds left in the game. • Vanderbilt strong safety CJ Heard leads the Commodores in tackles with 52. A 5-11, 210-pound Atlanta product who began his college career at Florida Atlantic, Heard also has made four tackles for loss, three sacks, broken up five passes, forced two fumbles and intercepted a pass. Special teams • Kentucky has not had consistently stellar punting in 2026, but Wilson Berry played a big role in the win at Oklahoma. The Australian uncorked a 58-yard, rugby-style kick that backed OU up to its 4-yard line with 2:43 left in the game. On the season, Berry is averaging 44 yards on eight punts and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line twice. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 8 of 11 on field goals in 2026 with a long make of 52 yards. • Vanderbilt punter Tyler Ebel is averaging 47 yards a kick and has pinned opponents inside their 20-yard line on 10 of 27 punts. Place-kicker Brock Taylor is 6 of 8 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 47 yards. For his college career, Taylor is 47 of 53 on field-goal tries with a long make of 57 yards. away.headline: Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky
away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. Vanderbilt’s initial injury report. Davin Chandler and Dontae Carter both questionable, Cayden Daniels probable and Josiah Broxton doubtful. pic.twitter.com/aDGBMzaMl8 Initial Vanderbilt Football Injury Report Before Trip to No. 12 Kentucky Skip to main content SI.COM More from Vanderbilt Commodores FOOTBALL The Commodores are currently on a four-game losing streak and are the only team in the conference to not win a SEC game this season. Contrast that with Kentucky, who is currently one of the hottest teams in the country and firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation. Vanderbilt had a somewhat lengthy injury report. The Commodores already knew going into the week it was going to be missing backup quarterback Blaze Berlowitz, cornerback Jaylin Lackey, defensive lineman Aaron Bryant and offensive lineman Gunner Givens. In recent weeks, Lea announced season-ending injuries to Givens and Bryant and a collarbone injury to Berlowitz. Vanderbilt will continue to be without linebacker Jamison Curtis, wide receiver Kahden Smith and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Lea will likely give updates on his guys Thursday from tonight's injury report as he usually does. At this point in the year, Vanderbilt is fairly banged up. But it has its final game this weekend before the bye week. This weekend’s game between Vanderbilt and Kentucky is significant to both teams in different ways. One team is looking to get its confidence back while the other is looking to not slip up as a big favorite at home. The Commodores and Wildcats kick off at 6:30 p.m. CT on SEC Network. Injuries to Ohio State’s Julian Sayin, Oregon’s Dante Moore, and UCLA’s Nico Iamaleava are among the most notable quarterbacks who have suffered injuries. One of those Big Ten teams fortunate to have the same starting quarterback they began the season with is the No. 16 USC Trojans, led by Jayden Maiava. The Trojans and Maiava will face another road test on Saturday night against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium. With Julian Sayin recently injured and the Trojans set to host the No. 3 Ohio State Buckeyes on Halloween night at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, USC has a golden opportunity to make a statement and boost its College Football Playoff chances with wins over the Wisconsin Badgers and the Buckeyes. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. At what point does Wisconsin give up on Wilkins as a starting-caliber offensive lineman this season? It's tried him at three spots — left tackle, right tackle and right guard — all of which have been problematic. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. When guys get dinged up, in particular Kawecki and moving Stylz back in there, we just felt like that was our best five," Fickell said this week . "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. With Kawecki probable as of the Wednesday injury report, he could return to center, meaning Blackmon could return to right guard. picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Can Wisconsin Ride Home Crowd to Win vs. No. 16 USC?
picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Can Wisconsin Ride Home Crowd to Win vs. No. 16 USC? Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Wisconsin missed out on a big opportunity to knock off its second top-15 team on the road last week, letting a winnable game at then-No. 12 UCLA slip through its fingers. The Badgers have a chance to right the ship and topple a team perched just outside the top-15 with the No. 16 USC Trojans coming to town. This is an absolutely enormous game for both coaches/programs in terms of what the expectations were ahead of each team's season. The noise at both schools would get significantly louder with a loss, their respective coaches' seats would get hotter . Ahead of the primetime showdown with USC, Badgers On SI's staff offers up roundtable predictions for the Week 8 clash: Seamus Rohrer, Editor Wisconsin's defense, which ranks No. 16 nationally allowing just 286.7 yards per game, gives them a chance against most teams. Whether or not that's a legitimate, fighting chance depends on what happens when they're on the sideline and quarterback Colton Joseph and the offense have the ball. I do expect the Badgers to be able to limit the Trojans' ground game. It's going to come down to whether or not Wisconsin can get off the field against one of the best third-down offenses in the country after it allowed a backup quarterback to pass for 150 yards on third down alone in Pasadena. When Joseph and company have the ball, what matters is how much Wisconsin can take advantage of a porous USC secondary, as well as how its struggling offensive front can hold up against some talented front seven players on the Trojans' defense, namely true freshman defensive end Luke Wafle. Ultimately, can the Badgers' offense keep pace with the high-flying Trojans? They haven't given me real reason to believe they can. Prediction: USC 27, Wisconsin 17 Wisconsin Badgers head coach Luke Fickell. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Drew Gentile, Staff Writer Last week, I believed in Wisconsin, and like the rest of the fanbase, was disappointed in the result. I'm not under the impression that it was a back-breaking loss, but it certainly diminished my confidence to a certain extent. All that said, UCLA is one of the best defenses in the country, while USC has been shaky on that side of the ball. For that reason, I think the offense bounces back, at least a little bit. My primary concern, however, is Jayden Maiava. Ty Dieffenbach had his way with Wisconsin's soft zone last week, and Maiava is in another stratosphere. Ultimately, I think this is a game the Badgers could win, but until I see a quality effort offensively, including success from Joseph through the air, I'm not betting on Wisconsin to keep up offensively for four quarters. Prediction: USC 24, Wisconsin 16 Jeremy Schneider, Staff Writer The UCLA loss last week stings, but it doesn’t mean Wisconsin can’t win this one. USC has struggled on the road since joining the Big Ten, and its defense is far from a reliable unit. That said, the Trojans can light up the scoreboard behind star quarterback Jayden Maiava. Wisconsin’s defense, particularly against the run, has been solid, but defensive coordinator Mike Tressel’s overreliance on soft zone coverage remains a concern. Ty Dieffenbach picked apart the zone to keep the chains moving last week. If a quarterback making his first FBS start can do that, what might a star like Maiava accomplish? Factor in Javan Robinson’s questionable status, and I’m concerned. Moving the ball should be easier against USC’s defense, but Colton Joseph still has plenty to prove with his arm against a higher-caliber opponent. This is a winnable game for Wisconsin, but I ultimately expect the Trojans to pull away late. Prediction : USC 28, Wisconsin 20 Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph (1) hands off to running back Abu Sama III (3). | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer Benjamin Worgull, Staff Writer There's a lot of truth to the old adage that "offense scores points, but defense wins championships." Wisconsin has a defense that has shown to be title worthy, allowing a Big Ten best 13.3 points per game and 284.0 yards per game during conference play. The problem is that UW's offense hasn't risen to that title level yet. While there was a blip of hope with its 31-point performance against Michigan State, UW slogged its way to a 213-yard evening against the Bruins, complete with a paltry 66 passing yards on six completions from Colton Joseph. Those numbers aren't going to beat anybody, especially a USC team that might be the best collection of individual talent the Badgers will see this season. The Trojans' defense isn't great (350 ypg, 63rd FBS) but they have shown the ability to slow the run (111 ypg, 32nd FBS). A one-dimensional offense rarely yields results, especially when the UW offense has a quarterback that hasn't truly found a groove yet. I feel like we were slightly duped by UW's four-game winning streak, which includes two Big Ten wins over two current winless conference teams. These next two games are huge opportunities for Fickell to show how his program is progressing, although I have a feeling they aren't going to be pretty. Prediction: USC 34, Wisconsin 21 Christian Borman, Staff Writer The Wisconsin offense's struggles last week at UCLA were definitely concerning. Things felt disjointed, and most of the production fell on Colton Joseph to keep things moving. The offensive line is still a work in progress, making problems of it's own. If this offense continues to be a problem and cannot sustain drives, the success of the game will land squarely on the shoulders of the defense. While I think the Badgers have a good defense, even the best defenses will wear down if they are always on the field. With the way the Trojans' offense can put up points, Wisconsin's best chance at winning this game will be taking the air out of the ball and dominating the time of possession. They need to get the running game going, whether it's with the running backs or Colton Joseph, and have long drives that end in points. The less Jayden Maiava is on the field, the better. But after last week at UCLA, there isn't a whole lot of evidence that shows me the Wisconsin offense is capable of doing that. For the third time in just over a month, USC travels east for a Big Ten road game, this time for prime-time action against Wisconsin at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wis., today at 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC). The lines on Kalshi have the Trojans as 2.5-point road favorites with the total at 49.5, and my USC vs. Wisconsin prediction and college football picks expect Lincoln Riley's program to stay undefeated on the road. For the rest of today's slate, see our Week 8 college football top picks and Brad Powers' Week 8 predictions . TOP PICK Who will win USC vs Wisconsin today? Pick: USC -2.5 USC has long faced criticism for its performances in cross-country road games under Lincoln Riley, but the Trojans beat Penn State by eight points in Week 6 at Happy Valley, covering as 1.5-point favorites. Fresh off a bye week, I like USC to cover -2.5 or better on the road against Wisconsin . The Badgers and Trojans are so different it's like they're playing completely different sports, and that favors USC. Wisconsin lost by double digits on the West Coast last week to a UCLA team led by a backup QB making his first start as a Bruin, and Jayden Maiava is a lot scarier than Ty Dieffenbach. Maiava ranks in the top 10 nationally in QBR (86.8) and is protected by one of the best offensive lines in the country, with the starting five credited with allowing just two sacks. If Wisconsin can't pressure Maiava, he'll pick the Badgers apart, and the Badgers won't be able to throw themselves back into the game. USC is also expected to have its most disruptive defensive player back, with Jahkeem Stewart listed as probable on the Big Ten injury report . Check the college football injury report for the latest before kickoff. For more spread plays, see our college football Week 8 picks against the spread . USC vs Wisconsin Over/Under pick: Over 49.5 This is the lowest game total of the season for USC, and that's because Wisconsin is the polar opposite type of team. (AP) — Austin Brawley returned an interception 56 yards for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter and New Mexico held on to beat North Dakota State 21-16 on Saturday night. Brawley's pick-6 gave the first-place Lobos (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West Conference) a 21-9 lead early in the fouth quarter. The senior safety had a 65-yard pick-6 in the previous home game — a 61-7 romp over UTEP. New Mexico marched 75 yards in six plays to start the game, scoring on Kiefer Sibley's 29-yard run for a 7-0 lead it never relinquished. Sibley finished with 91 yards on 13 carries. Scottre Humphrey scored on a 2-yard run with 10 seconds left in the first half for a 14-3 advantage. North Dakota State (6-2, 3-2) managed only 74 yards of offense and Drew Klein's 27-yard first-quarter field goal before halftime. Nathan Hayes finished off a 63-yard drive with a 15-yard touchdown pass to Reis Kessell, but Klein's extra-point kick was blocked and the Bison trailed 14-9. Brawley picked Hayes off and returned it for a touchdown and a 12-point lead. New Mexico has forced at least two turnovers in every game this season and leads the nation with 23. Hayes answered with a 4-yard touchdown pass to Mekhi Collins 10 plays later to cut it to 21-16 with 6:44 left, but New Mexico prevailed. Hayes had 198 yards on 17-for-33 passing but threw two interceptions. The Lobos have won four in a row following their only loss — a 14-6 setback to then-No. 24 Oklahoma on the road. away.blurb: New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday's. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native's work ethic in rehabbing his injury. "Joey, he's going to keep stepping up … I do think he's probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month," Eck said on Oct. 5. "Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way." If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that's been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers' all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday's game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM's 21-10 win over Hawaii. home.headline: Former USC TE could make season debut for Lobos against North Dakota State
home.blurb: New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday's. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native's work ethic in rehabbing his injury. "Joey, he's going to keep stepping up … I do think he's probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month," Eck said on Oct. 5. "Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way." If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that's been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers' all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday's game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM's 21-10 win over Hawaii. home.headline: Football-loving Olen, Lobos put final touches on preseason prep; Rytis Petraitis still injured
home.blurb: "So, from that standpoint, it's really beneficial. And then hopefully the fans are excited to come out and see it. Unfortunately in today's scheduling, if you want to see a Power Five team play in the Pit, it's probably going to be in an exhibition situation." Cal transfer Rytis Petraitis, the fifth-year forward who once played at Air Force, won't play Sunday against Arizona State, marking the second-consecutive exhibition game he'll be out with an injury. After last Sunday's win over the Cougars, Olen said: "I think if this were a regular-season game, he could have played. (He had) a little ankle sprain during practice. Just kind of taking some precaution to make sure we don't make it worse. We expect him to practice next week and be available Sunday (against Arizona State)." This past week, progress wasn't made. Olen confirmed to the Journal that imaging on the injured ankle confirmed it was just an ankle sprain as originally thought, just not one coming around as quickly as originally hoped and the 6-foot-7 forward is considered day-to-day, just not available for Sunday. The visiting Big 12 team has size the Lobos need to get better against, a Hall of Fame caliber head coach that will be key to prepare against and for fans it's one of the rare times in the current college athletics landscape for a big named team to agree to come into the Pit anymore. So clearly, with a 2 p.m. tipoff in the Pit on Sunday in the Pit, Olen won't be one of the 30,000-plus fans across the street watching the UNM Lobos football game against North Dakota State starting at 8 p.m. because he'll be watching film, loading up on game prep and getting a full night's rest, right? "Are you kidding me?" Olen fired back at a reporter Friday when asked if he was going to the football game. "Yeah, I'll be there. That's a huge game. I'm not going to miss that." Olen, you see, is a hoops junkie. But he's also a huge football fan — both of his childhood team Alabama and now of Jason Eck's Lobo football team. And it doesn't matter if he's watching with 30-35,000 of his closest friends or nobody at all around as his wife and kids are already in bed for the night. home.headline: Laubstein will miss rest of Lobos' season after suffering knee injury at Hawaii
home.blurb: After initially exhausting his eligibility, Laubstein was able to return to UNM for a sixth and final year via an NCAA waiver. A former junior college athlete, he successfully contended that at least one of his seasons spent at that level shouldn’t count toward his NCAA eligibility. James Laubstein, middle, provided a "lot of juice" for UNM, coach Jason Eck said. Mike Sandoval/Journal “Him being one of the oldest guys in the room, he taught me a lot,” Fa’avae said Tuesday. “(Laubstein) showed me the ropes and what to do, what not to do, how I should approach this, how I should approach that as a young quarterback. He taught me a lot of stuff I know today and always had my back, always helped me out. … It’s sad that got his season (taken) from him.” “We’ll have to have some element of (the) quarterback run involved,” he added. “But we gotta be careful because now two of our top four quarterbacks (Laubstein and Layne) coming into the year are out. So you don’t wanna get to less than that, you know?” Eck indicated receiver Shawn Miller (concussion) is not likely to play this week: “He’s just not coming along. He’s still battling symptoms and stuff, so he has not cleared the protocol (to return). And the longer it goes on, I think the more concerning it is because I think when you (show symptoms over an extended period of time), that kind of shows that it’s really affecting you. And that calls into question, is it safe for you to play?” Left tackle Cole Millward listed as questionable for Saturday's game Jump to main content NM Data Scoreboard Community Leaders Town Hall Series Business Submit Your Press Release Careers Journal Delivery Opportunities Run-first QB had 5 rushing TDs, the second-best mark for UNM James Laubstein, right, had a knack for finding the end zone with his legs. The 6-foot-3, 209-pound sixth-year player went down on a play in the second quarter and was later carted off the field with what Eck said was a patellar tendon injury.
